newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat hits new lows, Egypt buys French wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat hits new lows, Egypt buys French wheat.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were lower at midsession and new contract lows were set in the March and May with news over the weekend that Egypt bought French rather than U.S. wheat, the catalyst for the decline, traders said.
"Egypt buying wheat from France didn't help, that's bearish too..the increased global competition," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

The Egyptian state's main grain buyer said Sunday that Egypt bought 450,000 tonnes of wheat from France. U.S. exporters said Egypt bought the wheat at about $10.00 to $15.00 per tonne below U.S. prices.
CBOT March wheat sank to a new low of $4.11 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.20 set Friday. The new low for May is $3.97 per bushel, below the previous low of $4.04 also set Friday.
"It was a little disappointing in wheat with Egypt taking wheat out of France," agreed Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Funds and commercials sold wheat. Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of December while LIT America and Merrill Lynch Futures each sold two million Dec, the traders said.
At 1150 CDT, wheat was three to 8-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 8-1/2 at $4.15-1/2.
